FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 548
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Representative Matt Woods
Analyst: Jennifer Farish Date: 04/14/2025
House Bill 548 as introduced would decrease potential receipts to the Education Trust Fund by
an estimated $7.2 million annually for fiscal years 2026 through 2028 by exempting the
purchase of certain broadband equipment and supplies from projects funded or administered by
the Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs (ADECA) from state sales and
use tax for that time period.
Further, this bill could also decrease sales and use tax receipts to local governments by a
cumulative estimated maximum amount of $9.45 million annually, if all local governments
adopted the exemption provided by this bill.
ADECA's Alabama Connectivity Plan report from 2021 estimated the total cost to provide
certain statewide fiber connectivity at $4.5 billion over a 10-year period. ADECA attributed an
estimated 40% of project costs ($1.8 billion) to material.
